label: conj:sm-gauge-truncation
title: Standard-Model truncation: $\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1)$ in the archimedean gauge image
html:
We conjecture that the archimedean truncation of the categorical gauge symmetry — the image of the gauge action groupoid's symmetries at observable scales under the fibre functor \tau — contains the Standard Model gauge group: there is a group G_{\mathrm{arch}} receiving the truncation together with an injective group homomorphism

  \mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1)
  \;\hookrightarrow\;
  G_{\mathrm{arch}}.

The statement is deliberately containment, not isomorphism: the truncation may carry symmetry beyond the Standard Model factors, and the global form of the physical gauge group is (\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1))/\Gamma with \Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_6 undetermined by current experiment [tong2017]; an isomorphism claim would overstate both what the framework supports and what experiment fixes. A completed derivation would, conversely, have to predict \Gamma — a sharper falsifiable output than the containment itself.

The per-factor evidence is uneven, and the conjecture must be read against a structural constraint the framework has already proved. By the \mathrm{SU}(2)-emergence theorem, the gauge group of tensor automorphisms of a single quantum observable universe fibre is exactly \mathrm{SU}(2) (or its split real form). Consequently the embedding above cannot land in the gauge group of one fibre: any realisation of the \mathrm{SU}(3) and \mathrm{U}(1) factors must come from symmetry visible only at the groupoid level — multi-strand structure, framing data, and the interaction of distinct fibres — and a proposed realisation that places all three factors inside \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) of one fibre contradicts a proved theorem of the framework.

Current per-factor status. The \mathrm{SU}(2) factor is the proved fibre gauge group. For the \mathrm{U}(1) factor, the framing phase supplies a derived charge — the Coulomb charge Q = w/2 of the Coulomb-charge definition, evaluated at the tower's lowest level, since the writhe is preserved by conjugation but shifted by \pm 1 under stabilisation — and the writhe ladder matches the third isospin component I_3 across the nucleon doublet without a fitted scale (a comparison made at fixed strand number, so the level caveat does not weaken it); the hypercharge Y, however, is not obtained: the writhe map is falsified as a Y assignment (the proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ), and the precisely identified missing object is a second crossing invariant independent of the writhe. One candidate direction, recorded here without endorsement, is the ribbon-framing twist: on a framed link the twist and the writhe are exactly the two independent components of the self-linking number, and the helon model of Bilson-Thompson reads electric charge off ribbon twist in units of e/3 [bilson-thompson2005]; whether a per-strand framing datum exists categorically in this framework, and whether it survives the Gell-Mann–Nishijima and hypercharge-spectrum consistency batteries, is untested. For the \mathrm{SU}(3) factor no categorical derivation exists; what is available here is octonion and colour-complex-structure fragments consistent with a colour sector, but no construction of an \mathrm{SU}(3) action from the three-strand structure. The electroweak isotypic decomposition proposed in the G-action-on-substrate conjecture and the torus-link identifications of the electroweak triplet conjecture are themselves conjectural inputs, not support.

Finally, the truncation mechanism — the suppression of high-action morphisms at observable scales that would reduce the full categorical symmetry to an effective finite-dimensional group — is a heuristic with no derivation. The conjecture as formalised therefore asserts only the containment; it does not assert that the containment is induced by any particular freeze-out mechanism.
heading: Conjecture
